<a id="freq_table"></a>
## [`freq_table`](../../src/music/freq_table.asm#L6) `$9D73-$9EF2`

*words*

SID frequency of each quarter tone: 192 words, low byte first, 24 steps for each octave. The even entries are the semitones of an NTSC C64, from C0 (16.35 Hz). Each odd entry is the mean of the entries next to it. The last entry is $ffff. Note byte n uses entry 2n, so notes $00-$5f are valid. The tunes use notes $01-$54. The driver adds the base $9d73 as immediates at $9851/$9857 and $9be1/$9be7.

- **Read by:** [`start_note`](modules/music/tick.md#start_note) [`$9851`](../../src/music/tick.asm#L73), [`start_note`](modules/music/tick.md#start_note) [`$9857`](../../src/music/tick.asm#L76), [`effect_pitch_step`](modules/sound/effects.md#effect_pitch_step) [`$9BE1`](../../src/sound/effects.asm#L81), [`effect_pitch_step`](modules/sound/effects.md#effect_pitch_step) [`$9BE7`](../../src/sound/effects.asm#L84)

<a id="tempo_latches"></a>
## [`tempo_latches`](../../src/music/driver_tables.asm#L12) `$9F13-$9F34`

*words*

CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. Each value is 1000000 / rate, for 16 to 80 music ticks each second. A larger value gives a slower tune. The values assume a 1 MHz clock, so a PAL C64 plays the tunes 1.5% slower. No tune uses the entries 0-9.

- **Read by:** [`cmd_tempo`](modules/music/commands.md#cmd_tempo) [`$9A4C`](../../src/music/commands.asm#L224), [`cmd_tempo`](modules/music/commands.md#cmd_tempo) [`$9A52`](../../src/music/commands.asm#L226)
